Substituted by A.O., 1937, for 'L.G.'.

title: Superintendence and Revision

text.title: Provincial Government to make rules (continued)
rules: (b) Fixing the charges to be made by Conciliators for anything done by them under this Chapter.
(c) Determining what records and accounts shall be kept by Conciliators, and what returns shall be framed and furnished by them.

text.title: District Judge to inspect, etc.
rules: The District Judge shall inspect, supervise and control the proceedings, under Chapter II, Chapter IV and Chapter VI of this Act, of all Subordinate Judges and the proceedings of all Village-munsifs and Conciliators.

text.title: District Judge may withdraw case from Conciliator or Subordinate Judge
rules: (a) Transfer any application pending before a Conciliator to the file of any other Conciliator.

(b) Transfer from the Court of one Subordinate Judge to another any suit or any agreement pending before a Subordinate Judge under section 44 of this Act; or transfer to his own file any suit or other matter pending before the Court of any Subordinate Judge under Chapter II, Chapter IV or Chapter VI of this Act, and may dispose of the same as if he were a Subordinate Judge.

(c) Sit with Subordinate Judge as a Bench for trial of any case, stay the proceedings in any such suit or matter, and sit together with such Judge as a Bench to dispose of such suit or matter in accordance with the provisions of this Act.
If the members of any Bench sitting under this section differ in opinion, the opinion of the District Judge shall prevail.

text.title: Appointment of Assistant or Subordinate Judges to aid District Judge
rules: The Provincial Government may appoint an Assistant or Subordinate Judge to inspect and supervise, subject to the control of the District Judge, the proceedings of all Subordinate Judges under Chapter II, Chapter IV and Chapter VI of this Act, and of all Village-munsifs and Conciliators in any district or part of a district to which this Act applies.

notes: Substituted by the Dekkhan Agriculturists’ Relief Act, 1882 (22 of 1882), s. 14, for 'Chapter II and Chapter IV'.
Substituted by the Dekkhan Agriculturists’ Relief Act, 1881 (23 of 1881), s. 11, for the original section.
Inserted by the Dekkhan Agriculturists’ Relief Act, 1895 (6 of 1895), s. 13.
Substituted by Act 22 of 1882, s. 14, for 'Chapter II or Chapter IV'.
Substituted by Act 6 of 1895, s. 14, for the original section.
Substituted by A.O., 1937, for 'L.G.'.

title: Superintendence and Revision

text.title: Appointment of Assistant or Subordinate Judges to aid District Judge (continued)
rules: Provided that, if the Provincial Government thinks fit, the same Assistant or Subordinate Judge may be appointed for two or more such districts or parts of districts or districts and parts of districts.

The District Judge may, by order, confer upon any Assistant or Subordinate Judge appointed under this section, as regards any district or part of a district for which he is so appointed, all or any of the powers specified in the order which vest in the District Judge under section 51.

text.title: Of revision
rules: The District Judge may, for the purpose of satisfying himself of the legality or propriety of any decree or order passed by a Subordinate Judge in any suit or other matter under Chapter II, Chapter IV or Chapter VI of this Act, and as to the regularity of the proceedings therein, call for and examine the record of such suit or matter, and pass such decree or order thereon as he thinks fit.

Any Assistant Judge or Subordinate Judge appointed by the Provincial Government under section 52 may similarly, in any district for which he is appointed, call for and examine the record of any such suit or matter, and if he sees cause therefor, may refer the same, with his remarks thereon, to the District Judge, and the District Judge may pass such decree or order on the case as he thinks fit.
Provided that no decree or order shall be reversed or altered for any error or defect or otherwise, unless a failure of justice appears to have taken place.

text.title: Special Judge
rules: The Provincial Government from time to time may appoint an officer, as Special Judge, to discharge in the place of the District Judge all the functions of the District Judge under this Act in respect of the proceedings of all Subordinate Judges, Village-munsifs and Conciliators, and may cancel any such appointment.
Such Special Judge shall not, without the previous sanction of the Provincial Government, discharge any public function except those which he is empowered by this Act to discharge.
If any conflict of authority arises between the Special Judge and the District Judge, the High Court shall pass such order thereon consistent with this Act as it thinks fit.

No appeal shall lie from any decree or order passed by the District Judge under this Chapter, or by the Special Judge, or by an Assistant or Subordinate Judge appointed under section 52, or by a Bench, in any suit or proceeding under this Act.

notes: 1 Substituted by A.O., 1937, for 'L.G.'.
2 Substituted by the Dekkhan Agriculturists’ Relief Act, 1882 (22 of 1882), s. 14, for 'Chapter II or Chapter IV'.
3 The words 'and if the G. of I. so direct shall' replaced by the Devolution Act, 1920 (38 of 1920), s. 2 and Sch. I.
4 Substituted by A.O., 1937, for 'L.G.', which had been substituted by Act 38 of 1920, s. 2 and Sch. I, for 'G. of I.'.

title: Registration by Village-Registrars

rules: The District Judge or Special Judge, or any Assistant or Subordinate Judge or Bench, may refer to the High Court, under section 617 of the Code of Civil Procedure (XIV of 1882), any question of law, or usage having the force of law, or the construction of a document, arising in any case pending before him or it under this Chapter as if that case were a suit or an appeal pending before him or it.
In respect of every reference so made, sections 618 to 621 of the said Code, both inclusive, shall apply.

Provided that no reference shall be made under this section by any Assistant or Subordinate Judge, or by any Bench of which the District Judge or Special Judge is not a member, without the previous sanction of the District Judge or Special Judge, as the case may be.

text.title: Appointment of Village-registrars
rules: The Provincial Government may from time to time:
(a) appoint such persons as it thinks fit, whether public officers or not, to be Village-registrars for such local areas as it may from time to time prescribe;
(b) direct the Village-registrar for any local area to discharge the functions of a Village-registrar for any other local areas concurrently with the Village-registrars of such other local areas;
(c) delegate to any person, by name or in virtue of his office, the powers conferred on it by this section, and may cancel any such appointment, direction or delegation.

text.title: Instruments executed by agriculturist not to be deemed valid unless executed before a Village-registrar
rules: No instrument which purports to create, modify, transfer, evidence or extinguish an obligation for the payment of money or a charge upon any property, or to be a conveyance or lease, and which is executed after this Act comes into force by an agriculturist residing in any local area for which a Village-registrar has been appointed, shall be admitted in evidence for any purpose by any person having by law or consent of parties authority to receive evidence, or shall be acted upon by any such person or by any public officer, unless such instrument is written by, or under the superintendence of, and is attested by, a Village-registrar.

Provided that nothing herein contained shall prevent the admission of any instrument in evidence in any criminal proceeding, or apply to any instrument which is executed by an agriculturist merely as a surety, or to any instrument required by section 17 of the Indian Registration Act, 1877 (III of 1877), to be registered under that Act.

notes: 1 Inserted by the Dekkhan Agriculturists’ Relief Act, 1882 (22 of 1882), s. 15.
2 See now the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (5 of 1908), s. 113 and Order 46, rules 1 to 5.
3 Substituted by A.O., 1937, for 'L.G.'.
4 Inserted by the Dekkhan Agriculturists’ Relief Act, 1881 (23 of 1881), s. 12.
5 Inserted by the Dekkhan Agriculturists’ Relief Act, 1886 (23 of 1886), s. 9.
6 See now the Registration Act, 1908 (16 of 1908).

title: Registration by Village-Registrars

text.title: Execution of instruments before Village-registrar
rules: All instruments to which section 56 applies shall be written by, or under the superintendence of, a Village-registrar and executed in his presence.

When any persons intend to execute any instrument, all such persons shall appear before the Village-registrar appointed for the area in which the agriculturist, or when there are several agriculturists intending to execute the instrument, anyone of such agriculturists, resides.

The registrar, after satisfying himself as to the identity of the intending executants and receiving any prescribed fee or stamp, shall write the instrument, or cause the same to be written under his superintendence, and after reading it aloud or causing it to be so read in the hearing of the intending executants, shall require them to execute it in his presence.

Every instrument so written and executed shall at the time of execution be attested by the Village-registrar, and also, if any of the executants is unable to read the instrument, by two respectable witnesses.

For the purposes of this section, every executant shall appear in person before the Village-registrar; but every other party thereto may appear either in person or by any agent, being his relative, servant or dependent, duly furnished with a power-of-attorney executed and authenticated as prescribed by the Provincial Government, authorizing him to appear and act on his behalf.

text.title: Registration of instruments by Village-registrars
rules: Every Village-registrar shall keep a register of instruments executed before him in such form as shall, from time to time, be prescribed by the Inspector-General of Registration.

As soon as all the intending executants have executed any instrument before a Village-registrar, he shall make a copy of it or cause a copy to be made in his register, and shall deliver the original instrument to the party entitled to its custody.

Prior to delivery, the original instrument shall be endorsed under the Village-registrar’s signature, with the date of registration, the name and residence of the Village-registrar, and the volume and page of the register in which the instrument has been registered.

A certified copy of any entry in the register shall be granted by the Village-registrar, free of charge, on the application of any party to the instrument to which the entry relates, or of his agent or representative, and the copy shall be admissible as evidence of the contents of the instrument.

notes: 1 Substituted by Dekkhan Agriculturists’ Relief Act, 1881 (23 of 1881) for the original section.
2 Substituted by A.O., 1937, for 'L.G.'.
3 Inserted by Dekkhan Agriculturists’ Relief Act, 1882 (22 of 1882), s. 16.
4 Substituted by Act 23 of 1881, s. 14, for 'parties to any instrument have executed it'.
5 Words regarding certified copies replaced by Dekkhan Agriculturists’ Relief Act, 1886 (23 of 1886), s. 10(1).
6 Words regarding delivery endorsement replaced ibid., s. 10(2).
7 Insertion regarding certified copies ibid., s. 10(3).

title: Execution and Registration of Instruments

text.title: Consideration to be fully stated in every instrument executed before a Village-registrar
rules: In every instrument written by, or under the superintendence of, the Village-registrar, the amount and nature of the consideration, if any, shall be fully stated.

The Village-registrar shall also endorse upon the instrument a note under his hand, recording whether or not the transfer of the consideration stated therein, or of any part thereof, took place in his presence.

If the instrument modifies, or wholly or partly supersedes, a previous instrument, such previous instrument shall be produced before the Village-registrar and shall be fully described in the instrument to be executed, and shall be marked by the Village-registrar under his hand for identification.

text.section_number: Production of copy of previous instrument when to be permitted
rules: Provided that if it is alleged that any such previous instrument is on record or in the custody of a Court, or is lost, or has been destroyed, the Village-registrar, after ascertaining that such previous instrument was duly registered, may permit a certified copy thereof to be produced in lieu of the original.
In every such case the following procedure shall be observed:

rules.a: The contents of the certified copy shall be fully described in the modifying or superseding instrument, and the said copy shall be marked by the Village-registrar under his hand for identification, and shall then be delivered to the person who produced it.
rules.b: If the previous instrument is lost or destroyed, and the registered entry thereof is in his custody, the Village-registrar shall endorse on such entry a note under his hand as to the modification or supersession of the said instrument.
rules.c: If the previous instrument is in the custody of a Court, or if it is lost or destroyed, and the registered entry thereof is in the custody of another officer, the Village-registrar shall forward a certified copy of the entry in his register relating to the modifying or superseding instrument to such Court or officer, with a report explaining the circumstances, and such Court or officer shall, on receipt thereof, endorse on such previous instrument or registered entry a note as to the modification or supersession of the said instrument.

text.title: Registration under this Act to be deemed equivalent to registration under Indian Registration Act, 1877
rules: Every instrument executed and registered in accordance with the foregoing provisions shall be deemed to have been duly registered under the provisions of the Indian Registration Act, 1877 (III of 1877).

No instrument which ought to have been executed before a Village-registrar but has been otherwise executed shall be registered by any officer acting under the said Act, or in any public office, or shall be authenticated by any public officer.

notes: 1 Provisions by the Dekkhan Agriculturist’s Relief Act, 1902 (Bom. 1 of 1902), section 3.
2 See now the Registration Act, 1908 (16 of 1908).

title: Superintendence, Custody, and Registration of Instruments

text.title: Superintendence of Village-registrars and custody and destruction of their records
rules: The Provincial Government may appoint one or more officers to exercise, by themselves or their subordinates, general superintendence over all Village-registrars, and may make rules, or empower such officer(s) to make rules, consistent with this Act, for regulating the proceedings of the Village-registrars and for providing for the custody of their records.

The Provincial Government may, by order published in the official Gazette, declare that any documents other than wills remaining unclaimed in any registration office in any district or part of a district to which this Act applies, for a period exceeding two years, may be destroyed.

text.title: Exemption of instruments to which the Government or any officer of the Government is a party
rules: Nothing in this Act shall be deemed to require any instrument, to which the Government or any officer of the Government in his official capacity is a party, to be executed before a Village-registrar.

text.title: Power of Provincial Government to make rules
rules: The Provincial Government may, from time to time, make rules regulating the appointment, suspension, dismissal and remuneration of Village-registrars, and prescribing the fees to be levied by them.

text.title: Mode of execution by agriculturists of instruments required to be registered under Act III of 1877
rules: When an agriculturist intends to execute any instrument required by section 17 of the Indian Registration Act, 1877 (III of 1877), to be registered under that Act, he shall appear before the Sub-registrar within whose sub-district the whole or some portion of the property to which the instrument relates is situated.

The Sub-registrar shall write the instrument, or cause it to be written, and require it to be executed, and attest it and, if the executant is unable to read the instrument, cause it to be further attested, and otherwise act in accordance with the procedure prescribed for a Village-registrar by sections 57 and 59 of this Act, and shall then register the instrument.

notes: 1 Subs. by the Dekkhan Agriculturists’ Relief Act, 1895 (6 of 1895) s. 15, for original s. 61.
2 Subs. by A.O., 1937, for 'L.G.'.
3 Subs. ibid., for 'Govt. Gazette'.
4-5 Amendments clarifying 'the Government' and 'officer of the Government'.
6 Words relating to cooperative societies repealed and amended in subsequent acts.
7 Ch. VIIIA inserted by the Dekkhan Agriculturists’ Relief Act, 1886 (23 of 1886), section 11.
8 See now the Registration Act, 1908 (16 of 1908).

title: Receipts and Statements of Account

text.title: Agriculturists entitled to written receipts
rules: The person to whom any agriculturist makes any payment of money in liquidation of a debt shall, at the time of such payment, tender to such agriculturist, whether he demand the same or not, a written receipt for the amount of such payment.

If such payment is made under any instrument executed before a Village-registrar, the receipt shall, if the agriculturist so require, be endorsed on the copy of the instrument furnished to him under section 58.

text.title: Agriculturists entitled to annual statements of account
rules: Any agriculturist by whom any money is due under any instrument shall, on such date in each year as the Provincial Government, having regard to local custom, may from time to time fix by notification in the official Gazette, be entitled to receive on demand, from the person claiming under such instrument, a statement up to that date of his account under such instrument.

text.title: Agriculturists entitled to have account made up from time to time in a pass-book
rules: Any agriculturist in whose name an account is kept by any trader or money-lender shall be entitled to receive from such trader or money-lender, on demand, a pass-book; and to require, from time to time, that his account up-to-date be written therein and authenticated by the signature or mark of the said trader or money-lender.

An entry so made in any such pass-book of any payment made to the trader or money-lender shall be deemed to be equivalent, for the purposes of section 64, to the grant of a receipt for the amount so entered.
No person whose account has been written in a pass-book as required by this section shall be entitled also to demand an account under section 65.

text.title: Penalty for contravention of sections 64 to 66
rules: Any person who, in contravention of section 64, 65 or 66, refuses or neglects to tender a receipt or a statement of account or a pass-book, or to write, or cause to be written, any account or any part of an account in a pass-book, or to attest the same when so written, shall be punished for each such offence with fine which may extend to one hundred rupees.

notes: 1 See now the Registration Act, 1908 (16 of 1908).
2 The words regarding instruments to which any society registered under the Co-operative Credit Societies Act, 1904, is a party, repealed by Dekkan Agriculturists’ Relief (Amdt.) Act, 1912, s.3.
3 Subs. by A.O., 1937, for 'L.G.'.

sections.title: Pleaders, etc., excluded in certain cases
rules: No pleader, vakil or mukhtar, and no advocate or attorney of a High Court, shall be permitted to appear on behalf of any party to any case before a Conciliator or a Village-munsif.

Provided that any party may, on reasonable cause shown to the satisfaction of the Conciliator or Village-munsif, employ any relative, servant or dependent who is not, and has not previously been, a pleader, vakil or mukhtar, or an advocate or attorney of a High Court, to appear either conjointly with, or in lieu of, such party.
When a relative, servant or dependent appears in lieu of a party, he shall be furnished by him with a power-of-attorney defining the extent to which he is empowered to act.
notes: Substituted by the Dekkan Agriculturists’ Relief Act, 1881, s.15, for the original section 68.

sections.title: Power of Court to appoint pleader for agriculturist
rules: When in any suit or proceeding before a Subordinate Judge under this Act to which an agriculturist is a party, any pleader, vakil or mukhtar, or any advocate or attorney of a High Court, appears on behalf of any party opposed to such agriculturist, the Subordinate Judge, if he is of opinion that such agriculturist has no means of obtaining proper professional assistance, may, with the consent of such agriculturist, direct the Government pleader or any other fit person (who is willing so to do) to appear on his behalf.

sections.title: Mortgages, etc., to be valid only when written
rules: No mortgage, lien or charge of or upon any immoveable property belonging to an agriculturist shall be valid unless it is created by an instrument in writing under the hand of the person creating such mortgage, lien or charge.
Nothing in this section shall apply to any mortgage, lien or charge created by mere operation of law, or in favour of the Government or of any officer of the Government in his official capacity.

sections.title: Bar of application of section 258, Act XIV of 1882
rules: The last clause of section 258 of the Code of Civil Procedure (XIV of 1882) shall not apply to payments out of Court made in any proceeding under this Act, in any case where an acknowledgement by the judgment-creditor for the same is produced, or when the payment is either admitted by him or proved.
notes: Section 71 was inserted by the Dekkan Agriculturists’ Relief Act, 1895 (6 of 1895), s.16.
See now the Code of Civil Procedure 1908 (5 of 1908), Order 21, Rule 2.

sections.title: Rate of interest allowable on taking an account
rules: In taking an account under section 13 or any suit under this Act, where interest is chargeable, such interest shall be awarded at the following rates:
(a) The rate, if any, agreed upon between the parties or the persons (if any) through whom they claim, unless such rate is deemed by the Court to be unreasonable;

(b) If such rate is deemed by the Court unreasonable, or if no rate was agreed upon, or when any agreement between the parties or the persons (if any) through whom they claim, to set off profits against interest and assessment and similar charges without an account has been set aside by the Court, such rate as the Court may deem reasonable.
notes: Inserted by the Dekkhan Agriculturists’ Relief Act, 1895 (6 of 1895), s.17.

sections.title: Limitation
rules: In any suit for the recovery of money from a person who at the time when the cause of action arose was an agriculturist in any of the districts of Poona, Satara, Sholapur and Ahmednagar, the following periods of limitation shall be deemed substituted for those prescribed in the Second Schedule annexed to the Indian Limitation Act, 1877:
(a) When such suit is founded on a written instrument registered under this Act or any law in force at the date of execution of such instrument: twelve years;
(b) In any other case: six years;
exceptions: Does not apply to a suit for the recovery of money from a person who is a surety merely for the principal debtor if the principal debtor was not, at the time when the cause of action arose, an agriculturist in any of the districts aforesaid.
Does not revive the right to bring any suit which would have been barred by limitation if it had been instituted immediately before this Act came into force.
notes: Substituted by the Dekkan Agriculturists’ Relief Act, 1881, s.17, for original section 72.

sections.title: Decision as to whether person is an agriculturist, final
notes: Repealed by the Dekkan Agriculturists’ Relief Act, 1895 (VI of 1895), s.3.

sections.title: Certain agricultural produce exempted from attachment, etc.
rules: When the Collector has taken any immoveable property of a judgment-debtor or insolvent into his possession under section 22 or section 29, he may, by an order in writing, direct that any other such property not so taken shall be deemed to be reserved for the support of the judgment-debtor or insolvent and the members of his family dependent on him, and may rescind that order.

While any such order continues in force in respect of any immoveable property, agricultural produce grown on that property shall not be attached or sold in execution of a decree passed whether before or after this Act comes into force, and shall not vest in the receiver appointed in any insolvency proceedings.
notes: Inserted by the Dekkhan Agriculturists’ Relief Act, 1882, s.18.

sections.title: Civil Procedure Code to apply in Subordinate Judge’s Courts
rules: Except in so far as it is inconsistent with this Act, the Code of Civil Procedure (X of 1877) shall apply in all suits and proceedings before Subordinate Judges under this Act.

sections.title: Co-operative Credit Societies
rules: Except sections 2 and 21, the provisions of this Act shall not apply to any matter to or in which any society registered under the Cooperative Credit Societies Act, 1904 (X of 1904), is a party.
notes: Inserted by the Dekkhan Agriculturists’ Relief (Amdt.) Act, 1912 (Bom. 1 of 1912), s.1.

sections.title: Additional power to make rules
rules: The Provincial Government may, from time to time, make all such rules as it may deem necessary for carrying out the provisions herein contained.

sections.title: Rules to be published
rules: All rules made by the Provincial Government under this Act shall be published in the official Gazette, and shall thereupon, in so far as they are consistent with this Act, have the force of law.

source: The Requisitioned Land (Continuance of Powers) Ordinance, 1969
title: Preamble
text: An Ordinance to provide for the continuance of certain emergency powers in relation to requisitioned land, after the Defence of Pakistan Ordinance, 1965 ceases to have effect.

source: The Requisitioned Land (Continuance of Powers) Ordinance, 1969
title: Short title and commencement
text: This Ordinance may be called the Requisitioned Land (Continuance of Powers) Ordinance, 1969. It extends to the whole of Pakistan and shall come into force on the date on which the Defence of Pakistan Ordinance, 1965 ceases to have effect.

source: The Requisitioned Land (Continuance of Powers) Ordinance, 1969
title: Definitions
text: Definitions include 'appropriate Government', meaning the Federal or Provincial Government under whose authority the land has been requisitioned, and 'requisitioned land', meaning immovable property subject to requisition under the Defence of Pakistan Ordinance, 1965 at the commencement of this Ordinance.

source: The Requisitioned Land (Continuance of Powers) Ordinance, 1969
title: Continuance of requisitions
text: All requisitioned lands shall continue to be subject to requisition. The appropriate Government may use or deal with the land as it deems expedient and may release land from requisition at any time.

source: The Requisitioned Land (Continuance of Powers) Ordinance, 1969
title: Release from requisition
text: The Government may specify by written order the person to whom possession shall be given. Delivery of possession discharges the Government from liability. If the person cannot be found, a notice is to be affixed to the land and published in the official Gazette, at which point the land ceases to be requisitioned.

source: The Requisitioned Land (Continuance of Powers) Ordinance, 1969
title: Power to acquire requisitioned land
text: The Government may acquire requisitioned land by publishing a notice in the official Gazette. Land vests absolutely in the Government from the date of publication. Acquisition is allowed if works have been constructed at Government expense or if restoring the land would be excessive and the owner declines release without compensation. The Government's determination is final.

source: The Requisitioned Land (Continuance of Powers) Ordinance, 1969
title: Payment of compensation
text: Compensation for continued requisition is determined as per section 18 of the Defence of Pakistan Ordinance, 1965. For acquisition, compensation is by agreement or arbitration, considering market value at the date of requisition. Appeals may lie to the High Court except where awards are below amounts prescribed by rules. Government may make rules for implementation.

title: Power to obtain information
text: The Government may order any person to furnish information regarding requisitioned land. Failure to comply may be treated as an offence under sections 176 and 177 of the Pakistan Penal Code.

source: The Requisitioned Land (Continuance of Powers) Ordinance, 1969
title: Delegation of functions
text: The Government may delegate any power or duty under this Ordinance to an officer, under specified circumstances and conditions.

source: The Requisitioned Land (Continuance of Powers) Ordinance, 1969
title: Indemnity
text: No legal proceedings shall lie against any person or the Government for anything done in good faith under this Ordinance or its rules and orders.

source: The Requisitioned Land (Continuance of Powers) Ordinance, 1969
title: Savings
text: Anything done under the Defence of Pakistan Ordinance, 1965 (actions, liabilities, proceedings, appointments, or rules) shall be deemed done under this Ordinance, provided it is not inconsistent with its provisions.
